hegemony

hih-JEM-uh-nee -- stress on the second syllable, JEM. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hegemony is dominance or leadership of one group, state, or entity over others.

For two centuries the empire's naval hegemony let it dictate the terms of trade across three oceans.

Example

One tech company controls the app store, the operating system, and the advertising market, so every smaller firm must play by its rules to survive.

That kind of overarching dominance -- one power setting the terms that everyone else must follow -- is hegemony. The word describes leadership or control exercised by one group, state, or entity over all its rivals.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

dominance: Dominance is controlling power over others wherever it appears -- a chess master dominates a board, one store dominates a street. Hegemony is dominance grown large and settled: one state, group, or institution setting the terms every rival must live by. All hegemony is dominance; only entrenched, large-scale dominance is hegemony.

sway: Sway is loose, informal influence -- a critic holds sway over taste, a friend over your weekend plans. Hegemony is far heavier: not a voice people happen to heed but structural control, one power arranging the rules so that others have little real choice at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

subordination: the state of being under another's control

autonomy: independence and self-rule

Where it sits · how complete and secure the dominance is — ascendancy → hegemony → supremacy

ascendancy vs. hegemony: Ascendancy is lighter than hegemony -- ascendancy is an upper hand that may still be growing or temporary, while hegemony is entrenched dominance that sets the rules for everyone else.

supremacy vs. hegemony: Supremacy is even more absolute than hegemony: a hegemonic power leads and dominates but can still be challenged, while supremacy claims the unquestioned top position over all rivals.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hegemon-

root — hegemon-: leader (Greek hegemon, from hegeisthai 'to lead')

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: state or quality of (Greek -ia)

Put it together

Put it together: Hegemony comes from Greek hegemonia, 'leadership,' built on hegemon, 'leader.' In ancient Greece it named the leadership one city-state held over an alliance; today it names any arrangement where one power leads and the rest must follow.

Use the root in a new word: hegemonic

Use the root in a new word: hegemonic: Scholars described the studio's hegemonic control of early Hollywood, since it owned the theaters as well as the films.

Word Building

Word Choice

Hegemony is an academic word at home in history and politics essays: regional hegemony, cultural hegemony, economic hegemony. Use it for large-scale dominance of one state, group, or institution over others -- not for everyday bossiness between individuals.
